explanation: The inner conviction that Jesus is Lord and God raised him from the dead, which leads to salvation.
The confession or declaration where a person openly expresses their faith in Jesus as Messiah.
The seat of the human will and inner conviction where justification occurs through faith.
God's gift of eternal life and reconciliation with him, available to all who call on the name of the Lord.
The title used for Jesus Christ, recognized as God and Messiah in Christianity.
The invocation or prayer where a person asks for God's grace through the name of Jesus.
Divine laws, especially those given to Israel, which required perfect obedience for justification.
The state of being in harmony with God, achieved not by works but through faith in Christ.
The good news of God's salvation and grace available to both Jews and Gentiles.
